practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 85(1) of the Constitution empowers the President to summon each House of Parliament. The maximum gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum permissible gap between two successive sessions of Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 85, Parliament must meet at least twice a year, with the gap between two sessions not exceeding six months.

practiceQuestions.q: Which device of parliamentary proceedings is an Indian innovation, not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure?
practiceQuestions.sol: Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation existing since 1962. It is not mentioned in the official Rules of Procedure.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the quorum required to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament?
opts: One-tenth of the total members of each House
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 100(3), the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House is one-tenth of the total number of members of that House.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the power to prorogue the House of Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: The President issues a notification for prorogation of the session of the House, unlike adjournment which is done by the presiding officer.

practiceQuestions.q: Which type of question requires an oral answer on the floor of the House and is distinguished by an asterisk mark?
practiceQuestions.sol: A Starred Question requires an oral answer and hence supplementary questions can follow. It is distinguished by an asterisk.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary distinction between adjournment and prorogation?
opts: Adjournment ends the session, prorogation ends the sitting
Adjournment suspends work in a sitting, prorogation terminates the session
Only the President can adjourn the House
practiceQuestions.sol: Adjournment terminates only a sitting of a House, while prorogation terminates both the sitting and the session of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following motions requires a support of at least 50 members to be admitted in the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: An Adjournment Motion needs the support of 50 members for admission because it interrupts the normal business of the House to discuss a matter of urgent public importance.

practiceQuestions.q: At what time does the Question Hour normally begin in the Lok Sabha?
practiceQuestions.sol: The first hour of a parliamentary sitting is termed Question Hour, which normally begins at 11:00 AM every day.

practiceQuestions.q: Who decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill under Article 110?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final and unquestionable authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is a No-Confidence Motion unique compared to other executive-accountability motions in the Lok Sabha?
opts: It requires setting out specific grounds or reasons for its adoption.
It can be moved against an individual minister as well as the entire council.
It needs no reasons to be stated, and if passed, the entire Council of Ministers must resign.
It can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: A No-Confidence Motion does not need to state reasons, can only be moved in the Lok Sabha, and its passage results in the fall of the government.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the 'Lame-duck session' affect the composition and functioning of the Parliament?
opts: It refers to the session where newly elected members participate before old members leave.
It refers to the last session of the existing Lok Sabha after a new Lok Sabha has been elected, where many members fail to get re-elected.
It is a special session called by the President when there is a hung parliament.
It is a session where only financial business is transacted without quorum.
practiceQuestions.sol: Lame-duck session refers to the last session of the current Lok Sabha after some members have failed to get re-elected to the new Lok Sabha. Such members are called lame-ducks.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to Bills pending in the Lok Sabha when the House is prorogued by the President?
opts: Pending bills lapse only if they originated in the Rajya Sabha.
Pragoration does NOT affect the lapsing of bills; pending bills remain active for the next session.
Only Government bills lapse, while Private Member bills survive.
practiceQuestions.sol: Prorogation terminates a session, but NOT the House itself. Hence, pending bills (in both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) do not lapse upon prorogation. Only dissolution causes bills to lapse under specific conditions.

practiceQuestions.q: Under what constitutional condition does the Parliament acquire the power to legislate on items in the State List without a constitutional amendment?
opts: If the Prime Minister recommends it.
If the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a 2/3rd majority present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest.
If the Lok Sabha passes a simple majority resolution.
If the Supreme Court directs parliament to do so.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 249 enables Parliament to legislate on a State List subject if Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Adjournment Motion considered an extraordinary device in parliamentary proceedings?
opts: It requires the approval of the Supreme Court before introduction.
It curtails the normal business of the House to focus exclusively on a definite matter of urgent public importance.
It can only be introduced by the Leader of the Opposition.
Its passage leads to the immediate dissolution of the Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Adjournment Motion is extraordinary because it interrupts the normal business of the House to discuss an urgent public issue, and thus has elements of an indirect censure against the government.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the structural consequence of a Cut Motion being passed in the Lok Sabha during the budget session?
opts: It amounts to a vote of no-confidence, leading to the resignation of the government.
The budget is automatically scrapped and must be re-drafted by the NITI Aayog.
Only the specific ministry whose grant is cut must resign.
It has no financial impact; it is purely symbolic.
practiceQuestions.sol: The passage of a cut motion reflects a lack of majority support for specific budgetary demands, which implies a loss of confidence in the government, necessitating its resignation.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best defines a 'Private Member's Bill'?
opts: A bill introduced by any minister who is not a cabinet member.
A bill introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a minister.
A bill discussed behind closed doors without public media access.
A bill that can only be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
practiceQuestions.sol: Any MP who is not a minister is classified as a private member. A bill introduced by such a member is a Private Member's Bill, distinct from a Government Bill.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of the 'Censure Motion' moved in the Lok Sabha?
opts: To compel the government to resign immediately.
To censure the Council of Ministers or an individual minister for specific policies or failures.
To postpone the business of the House for discussing natural disasters.
To question the Speaker on matters of procedural bias.
practiceQuestions.sol: A Censure Motion must state the reasons for its adoption and can be moved against the entire council or individual ministers. Unlike a no-confidence motion, its passage does not force the government to resign.

practiceQuestions.q: How does a Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament resolve a legislative deadlock?
opts: By consensus of party leaders in a closed room.
By a simple majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.
By a two-thirds majority of members of Rajya Sabha.
By presidential veto overriding parliamentary stalemate.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 108, a joint sitting is presided over by the Speaker and decided by a simple majority of members present and voting, combining the numerical strength of Lok Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the consequence of the Rajya Sabha rejecting a constitutional amendment bill passed by the Lok Sabha?
opts: A joint sitting is convened by the President.
The bill lapses because constitutional amendment bills require passage in both Houses separately without joint sitting provision.
The Prime Minister can dissolve the Lok Sabha and order fresh elections.
The Supreme Court decides the fate of the bill.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 368 requires a constitutional amendment bill to be passed by each House separately. There is no provision for a joint sitting in case of a deadlock on a constitutional amendment bill.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sessions of Parliament:
1. The power to convene a joint sitting of both Houses is vested in the President under Article 108.
2. All pending bills in the Lok Sabha lapse on the dissolution of the House, including those transmitted from the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting summoned by the President. Statement 2 is correct: Dissolution of Lok Sabha causes all pending bills in Lok Sabha to lapse, whether originating there or transmitted from Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Question Hour:
1. It is the first hour of a parliamentary sitting exclusively reserved for asking and answering questions.
2. Starred questions require written answers and supplementary questions cannot be asked on them.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Question Hour is the first hour of sitting. Statement 2 is incorrect because Starred questions require oral answers and allow supplementary questions, whereas Unstarred questions require written answers.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Parliamentary Motions:
1. A No-Confidence Motion can be moved against the entire Council of Ministers or an individual minister.
2. An Adjournment Motion needs the support of 50 members for its admission in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because a No-Confidence Motion can only be moved against the entire Council of Ministers, not an individual minister. Statement 2 is correct: An Adjournment Motion requires 50 members' support for admission.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the lapsing of bills:
1. A bill pending in the Lok Sabha that has been passed by the Rajya Sabha does NOT lapse on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
2. A bill pending in the Rajya Sabha which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha does NOT lapse on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: A bill pending in Lok Sabha (even if transmitted from Rajya Sabha) lapses on dissolution. Statement 2 is correct: A bill pending in Rajya Sabha that was NOT passed by Lok Sabha does NOT lapse on dissolution.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Budget and Cut Motions:
1. Policy Cut Motion represents disapproval of the policy underlying a demand and reduces the demand to Re. 1.
2. Token Cut Motion aims to ventilate a specific grievance within the sphere of responsibility of the Government of India and reduces the demand by Rs. 100.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate definitions of Policy Cut Motion (reducing amount to Re. 1) and Token Cut Motion (reducing amount by Rs. 100).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Prorogation and Adjournment:
1. Prorogation is done by the presiding officer of the House, whereas Adjournment is done by the President.
2. Adjournment terminates a sitting of the House, while Prorogation terminates a session of the House.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because it is reversed: Prorogation is done by the President, and Adjournment is done by the presiding officer. Statement 2 is correct.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Joint Sitting of Parliament:
1. The provision of joint sitting applies to ordinary bills and financial bills (under Article 117), but NOT to Money Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills.
2. The quorum to constitute a joint sitting is one-tenth of the total number of members of both Houses combined.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Joint sitting applies to ordinary and financial bills, but Money Bills and Constitutional Amendment Bills cannot have a joint sitting. Statement 2 is correct: Quorum for joint sitting is 1/10th of the total members of both Houses.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Parliamentary Privileges:
1. Parliamentary privileges are enjoyed by individual members as well as by each House of Parliament collectively.
2. These privileges are derived exclusively from conventions of the British House of Commons, with no mention in the Indian Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Privileges are both individual and collective. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 105 of the Indian Constitution explicitly mentions parliamentary privileges.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the President's Address to Parliament:
1. The President addresses both Houses of Parliament assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the commencement of the first session of each year.
2. The President's address outlines the policies and programmes of the incoming government and is debated by both Houses through a motion of thanks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct and accurately describe the provisions under Article 87 regarding the President's special address and the subsequent Motion of Thanks.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the languages used in Parliament:
1. The Constitution stipulates that business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or in English exclusively, barring any exceptions.
2. The Presiding Officer can permit a member of the House to address the House in their mother tongue if they cannot adequately express themselves in Hindi or English.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 120 states that parliamentary business is conducted in Hindi or English, but the presiding officer can permit members to speak in their mother tongue. Statement 2 is therefore correct.
